question: Assess whether NAB's FY25 Business & Private Banking growth was value-accretive rather than growth bought at the expense of margin or credit quality. Reconcile lending, revenue and cash-earnings growth with the NIM, impairment-charge and sector/NPL disclosures, and identify what is broad-based versus single-name driven.
answer:
**Verdict: broadly value-preserving rather than clearly value-accretive.** FY25 B&PB cash earnings rose 1.6% to $3,330m on revenue up only 2.1%, while business lending grew 7.3% and deposits 6.6% — volume was partly bought with margin (NIM −8bps to 3.01%) and returns per dollar of balance sheet slipped. Credit quality deteriorated, but the P&L charge did not (charge/GLAs −1bp to 0.19%), and the NPL rise is largely two well-secured Agri names.

**Reconciliation.** Lending→revenue: business lending $155.0bn→$166.3bn (+7.3%), housing $103.3bn→$109.3bn (+5.8%), deposits $223.1bn→$237.9bn (+6.6%); NII +2.8% to $7,499m; other operating income −2.9% (underlying fees −$9m/−0.9%). Revenue lagged volumes because NIM fell 8bps on "competitive pressures impacting both the business and housing lending portfolios, as well as higher deposit costs including mix impacts due to term deposit growth". At group level, lending margin fell only 1bp, with "favourable portfolio mix from stronger higher yielding business lending growth" — the business growth is mix-accretive to the group. Revenue→cash earnings: expenses +2.9% (underlying +$102m/3.2% on extra bankers and technology) lifted cost-to-income 30bps to 37.9%; impairment +$6m; cash earnings +$53m (+1.6%). Returns: cash earnings/average assets 1.25% (−5bps), /average RWA 2.18% (−1bp), with RWA +9.0% — partly "deterioration in asset quality".

**Credit quality.** Divisional impaired assets/GLAs +10bps to 0.49% and default-but-not-impaired +31bps to 2.05%; group NPE +18.2% ($1,864m) to $12,094m (1.55% of GLAs, +16bps), "mainly driven by deterioration in the Business and Private Banking business lending portfolio"; individually assessed provisions +53.8% to $1,163m driven by B&PB business lending. Yet the divisional charge/GLAs improved 1bp to 0.19% (2H25 0.21% vs 2H24 0.25%), helped by collective releases (group: $215m target-sector FLA release; collective/CRWA 1.33%, −14bps).

**Broad-based vs single-name.** Growth is broad-based: "growth in business lending across a broad range of sectors"; segment growth Agri +3.5%, Health +5.9%, CRE +7.4%, Other +10.4%; SME share 21.7%. Deterioration is substantially single-name: two large well-secured Agri customers contribute 21bps of the 3.22% B&PB business-lending NPL ratio; excluding them it fell 3bps to 3.01%, with "stable to improving NPL outcomes in 2H25 for most sectors".

**Not settled:** the Agri exposures' dollar size; any B&PB NPE dollar split; the price-vs-mix split of the 8bps NIM decline.

key_facts.fact: B&PB FY25 cash earnings $3,330m, +1.6% vs FY24 ($3,277m), on a cash (non-IFRS) basis with restated comparatives.
B&PB FY25 net operating income $8,531m (+2.1%); net interest income $7,499m (+2.8%); other operating income −2.9% with underlying fees −$9m/−0.9%.
B&PB business lending +7.3% to $166.3bn, housing +5.8% to $109.3bn, deposits +6.6% to $237.9bn (Sep 25 v Sep 24).
B&PB NIM fell 8bps to 3.01% on competitive pressures in business and housing lending and higher deposit costs including term-deposit mix, partly offset by replicating-portfolio earnings.
Group lending margin fell only 1bp, with favourable mix from stronger higher-yielding business lending growth relative to housing.
B&PB credit impairment charge $529m (+1.1%); charge/GLAs annualised 0.19% (−1bp); 2H25 $292m/0.21% vs 2H24 $322m/0.25%, with 2H25 increase driven by business lending.
B&PB cash earnings on average assets 1.25% (−5bps) and on average RWA 2.18% (−1bp); RWA +9.0% to $159.2bn, mostly business lending growth plus asset-quality deterioration.
Group NPE +18.2% ($1,864m) to $12,094m, 1.55% of GLAs (+16bps), mainly driven by B&PB business lending deterioration; default-but-not-impaired ratio +7bps to 1.26% mainly B&PB business lending.
B&PB impaired assets/GLAs 0.49% (+10bps); default but not impaired 2.05% (+31bps).
Two large well-secured Agri customers add 21bps to the 3.22% B&PB business-lending NPL ratio; excluding them the ratio fell 3bps to 3.01%, with stable-to-improving 2H25 NPL outcomes in most sectors.
Business lending growth is broad-based across sectors (Agri +3.5%, Health +5.9%, CRE +7.4%, Other +10.4%); SME lending share 21.7% at Sep 25.

Group individually assessed provisions +53.8% to $1,163m driven by B&PB business lending; collective provisions −3.2% to $5,002m including a $215m target-sector FLA release; collective/CRWA 1.33% (−14bps).

limitations: The two large Agri customers are not named and their dollar NPL size is not disclosed; only their 21bps contribution to the B&PB business-lending NPL ratio is printed.
No B&PB-specific NPE dollar table was read; the group NPE driver attribution to B&PB is qualitative.
The split of the 8bps B&PB NIM decline between lending price competition and deposit cost/mix is qualitative only.
All FY24 comparatives are restated for PB↔B&PB portfolio transfers and an expense-presentation change, so growth rates are on restated bases.
Presentation segment growth rates are on a customer-segment basis, not industry, with Sep 24 balances restated.
Cash earnings is a non-IFRS, unaudited measure; divisional figures are on that basis, not statutory.
